hypotheses.cause: The original has an intersection label M at the crossing of CP and FE, but label detection did not extract it. The GES has no label object for M and no binding to a point.
hypotheses.evidence: The GES LABEL/label list contains A, B, C, D, E, F, P only. point_08 at (681.87, 433.36) is the computed intersection of seg_CP and seg_FE (both 'on_segment' candidates) but has no label. The audit shows ges_point_labels and drawn_labels both lack M. The critic's label_error cites M 'just below-left of the crossing', but the critic is a heuristic visual judgment and may be wrong about the label's existence.

hypotheses.cause: The critic's 'stub crossing AF at P, perpendicular to AF' is probably the ~28 px overhang of segment CP beyond P, not a separate spurious object. The render's extended C-P line (Q at (-0.212, 0.898) past P) would cross AF at P, which matches the description.
hypotheses.evidence: The GES has no separate segment perpendicular to AF near P. The unresolved list says 'C-P extends ~28 px beyond P; kept as overhang, unclear if intended to end at P.' The code comment 'Extended C-P line end (through P)' confirms the overhang is deliberate. The critic says the original has no overhang, which conflicts with the geometry agent's unresolved note, so the original's behavior at P is not established.

hypotheses.cause: The dashed PE stroke is heavier than the original's fine dashes, and the stroke width is not recorded in the GES, so this cannot be checked from the GES alone.
hypotheses.evidence: seg_09 (dashed, 12 thin ink dashes, chain 285.8 px) is detected from the image, while seg_PE (dashed, geometry_agent candidate) has a ~9 px start offset from the CP line and different endpoints (seg_09 runs from (461.67, 238.05) to (312.55, 547.38); seg_PE from (457.86, 247.08) to (315.51, 541.06)). The GES gives no stroke-width or dash-pattern measurement for either segment. The code uses a global line width of 1.1pt for all strokes, so the heavier look must come from comparing visual stroke thickness in the image, which the GES does not provide.
